transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is defending himself amid a wave of criticism.
He held a rare press conference, his first in six months, amid impeachment efforts that
have started in the House of Representatives, NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
The press conference comes a day after Republican Congressman Thomas Massey introduced articles
of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth over his handling of the war in Iran and other
military operations.
Hegseth began by addressing the move to impeach him, calling it a "political spectacle."
It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it.
Congressman Massey has accused Hegseth of violating laws against harming civilians and
violating the Constitution and federal law by ignoring the will of Congress to carry
out the war in Iran, among other concerns.
President Trump defended Hegseth on social media after he spoke.
The House is expected to vote on the impeachment effort in the coming days.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
The cost of regular gasoline in the U.S. has fallen below $4 a gallon for the first time
since mid-summer, but inflation remains an issue affecting the entire economy.
NPR's Scott Horsley has the story.
AAA says the average price of regular gas has dipped to $3.98 a gallon, that's down
about 39 cents from a month ago, but still very high for this time of year.
A separate report from the Labor Department shows inflation in October was higher than
forecasters expected.
Consumer prices rose by four-tenths of a percent last month.
Housing costs accounted for about a third of the monthly increase.
Grocery prices were also sharply higher in October.
Prices were not collected last October during the government shutdown, so there's no official
figure for inflation over the last 12 months, and let's say prices continue to climb faster
than average wages though, so the typical worker is falling behind.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
AAA says gas prices are below $4 a gallon for the first time since July.
Russian, American, and Ukrainian negotiators have wrapped up their first day of talks in
Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the war against Ukraine.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports there has been some changes in the last talks from six
months from nine months ago.
For Russia, the midterms are not good news.
Things are going very well with the Trump administration that recently waived sanctions
on diesel, which allows Russia to finance its war.
So analysts are saying Putin may try to squeeze as much as he can out of the Trump administration
before the new Congress comes in.
Russia did enjoy recent Trump administration actions, including waived sanctions on diesel.
The sale of that oil has helped Russia to finance its war against Ukraine.
On Wall Street, Outlast checked the Dow is down 341 points.
The S&P 500 is down more than 64, while the Nasdaq is down more than 336 points.
You're listening to NPR News.
The Food and Drug Administration is requiring drugmakers to add a new warning to the labels
of popular GOP-1 drugs.
NPR's Sydney Lumpkin reports the warning involves a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent
vision loss.
The FDA says there's potentially an increased risk of a rare eye problem associated with
GLP-1 medications.
It's called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NION, and it's caused
by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve.
The condition is usually painless and results in vision loss in one eye that can be permanent.
The FDA is requiring drug companies making GLP-1s to add information about NION to the
warning sections of their labels.
GLP-1 drugs include Ozempic and Wagovi, as well as Manjaro, Zepbond, and Foundeo.
They also include drugs like Trulicity and Victoza.
Patients should be aware of the risk and contact their doctors right away if they experience
vision symptoms while taking these drugs.
Sydney Lumpkin, NPR News.
Superman, Batman, and the rest of the DC heroes are getting a new boss.
James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-chief executives of DC Studios.
The change was announced by Skydance, which acquired Warner Brothers Discovery.
Gunn and Safran's tenure included the release of the latest Superman movie.
The new head of DC Studios will be Jeremy Latcham.
He will take over as president and as chief creative officer starting on December 1st.
I'm Lyndy Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defends himself at rare press conference amid House impeachment push
AAA reports national average regular gas price falls below $4 a gallon, first time since July
October inflation report from Labor Department comes in higher than forecasters expected
US, Russian, and Ukrainian negotiators end first day of Abu Dhabi talks on ending Ukraine war
Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq fall in midday trading on Wall Street
FDA requires warning label on GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Zepbound for rare eye condition NION
James Gunn and Peter Safran step down as co-CEOs of DC Studios; Jeremy Latcham named successor
